name: Millhaven end house and cellar (the hatch)
region: Millhaven, east side, where the garden walls give out; back wall on the lane

sensoryProfile.sight: One room, a box bed against the far wall (dragged out of place across the floor leaving two long pale scrapes), a hearth with grey ash, a table with two bowls grown over with soft grey fur and a spoon standing upright in one. Under the bed's place a square hatch flush with the boards with an iron ring, bolted from below. The cellar: a clay-dug room with a ladder, a bin of turnips (spilled), a barred cellar slot a hand high and two hands long in the back wall right under the beams, with a crust of dirt on the sill.
sensoryProfile.sound: A child's scraped whisper; the bolt scraping; water trickling through the crack; the lantern hissing on the table.
sensoryProfile.smell: Cold earth, damp, piss and turnips; staleness 'breathed over and over'.
sensoryProfile.touch: Cold clay; damp; the black-cold of a child's bare ankle.
sensoryProfile.atmosphere: Held-breath intimacy against the rest of the village's emptiness; the only living place in Millhaven.

establishedFacts.fact: The end house had been swept once by Cyndia and called empty; the bed hid the hatch. Someone had dragged the box bed over the hatch from above (the girl's father, apparently) and the child had bolted it from below.

The cellar slot looks out on the lane at about the height of a dog's nose; a child standing on the turnip bin could put her face to it; this is how the girl saw feet 'going past', toes pointing away from the mill toward Pell's.
The bowls on the table show 'five days at the most' of mould (Sylvanas's inference).
The cellar reads contaminated 'in the ground, the same as everywhere'; nothing that had been in it was carrying it.

eventsHere.event: Neral hears breathing, talks the girl out, and brings her up; Jaina checks the cellar; the girl's account is taken.
